title: not certainty
tomorrow: Elijah: not the wind, not the earthquake

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Psalms. A hundred and fifty songs, and plenty of them shouting. Your line: you can say anything to him. Did you say one true thing? Day seventeen.

Some people seem to have faith like a wall. Solid, certain, never shaken. And if you're not like that, it's easy to decide faith isn't for you. You have questions. You have bad weeks. Some mornings you're not sure of anything. Here's a scene from Mark's Gospel. A father brings his sick son to Jesus. He's exhausted. He's tried everything. He says: if you can do anything, help us. Jesus tells him all things are possible to the one who believes. And the father cries out one of the most honest lines in the Bible: "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief." Both at once. Today's word.
screen: `FAITH LIKE A WALL?` → `A FATHER, OUT OF OPTIONS.` → `"I BELIEVE; HELP MY UNBELIEF."`

segments.voice: Faith. The Greek word is pistis, and it's less about certainty than about trust. It's the word for trusting a friend, or being faithful to one. It can mean loyalty. You have faith in someone the way you have faith in a bridge: not because you've proved it, but because you're willing to put your weight on it. Remember day one? Amen, from the Hebrew root for firm, solid. Same idea. Now, how much of it do you need? Matthew tells the same story as Mark. Afterward, the disciples ask Jesus why they couldn't help the boy themselves. And he says: "If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove." A mustard seed. Smaller than a peppercorn. He doesn't say: if you had enormous faith. He says: if you had even this much. The mountain is big. The seed is tiny. The point is the seed. The letter to the Hebrews has another famous line: "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen." Not seen. In that line, faith is what you have exactly when you can't see. Which means doubt isn't simply its opposite. Christian writers across the centuries have said that doubt is often where faith lives, not where it dies. The father in Mark didn't bring a perfect faith. He brought a half-sure, crying, both-at-once faith, and the story doesn't send him away. Jesus heals the boy. Christians say that's enough to start with. On an ordinary Tuesday, faith isn't a feeling of certainty. It's one small step of trust, taken while you're still not sure.
screen: `PISTIS — TRUST, NOT PROOF.` · `A MUSTARD SEED.` · `THE EVIDENCE OF THINGS NOT SEEN.` · `DOUBT ISN'T THE OPPOSITE.` · then, large: `SMALL IS ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice. Seventy-five seconds. If there's something tiny nearby, a grain of rice, a seed, a crumb, put it in your palm. If not, just open your hand. Sit, and breathe. Think of one thing you're unsure about. Don't solve it. Just admit it. Now think of one small thing you do trust. The floor holding you up. The next breath coming. One person. Let that small thing be enough, for now. If you pray, the father's words are there for you: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief. The bell holds the time.
Faith. Pistis. Not certainty: trust, even the size of a seed. Seventeenth word.
Your line: small is enough. Today, take one small step on something you're unsure about. One message, one call, one yes. Day seventeen.

screen: `DAY 17 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: ELIJAH: NOT THE WIND, NOT THE EARTHQUAKE.`

howItsDone: Christians describe faith as trust in God more than certainty about everything, and many pray the father's line from Mark, "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief," in times of doubt.

myth: in the Bible, faith means being certain
the Greek pistis is trust and faithfulness: putting your weight on something you can't prove.

he said faith as small as a grain of mustard seed.

fork.setup: your son has been sick for years. Jesus says all things are possible to the one who believes. you're not sure you do. what do you say?
options: "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief."
fork.reveal: the father says both at once, belief and unbelief, and the story doesn't turn him away: Jesus heals the boy.

original.note: Greek. faith, trust, faithfulness. the same word covers trusting someone and being loyal to them.

trapdoor: what you thought: faith means being certain, with no doubts.
what it means: trust — putting your weight on something, even a mustard seed's worth.
what a scholar hears: in ordinary Greek pistis meant trust, a pledge, loyalty. Hebrews 11:1 defines faith by what is "not seen."

notes: Matthew 17:14–20 and Mark 9:14–29 are treated as the same story (the boy the disciples couldn't heal); standard, but confirm.
'Doubt is often where faith lives' is attributed generally to Christian writers across the centuries, not to any one; a Keeper may want to soften or cite.
The practice offers Mark 9:24 as a line to pray 'if you pray' — a real scripture line, not a new prayer.
